subject: Board snapshot: outcomes and contracting lane
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Claire Holt <claire.holt@stellarus.com>, Michael Choi <michael.choi@stellarus.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Dec 2026 15:24:00 -0800
Subject: Board snapshot: outcomes and contracting lane

Hi Claire / Michael —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap for your leadership pack and the next contracting/checkpoint items we discussed. I kept this intentionally short so you can paste into a board memo if helpful.

Key business outcomes you flagged
- Reduce inference latency variability for live recommendations (current 95th pct spikes ~450–600ms). Target: consistent sub-200ms 95th for customer-facing flows.
- Improve unit economics for high-volume scoring (10M+ requests/month expected next year). Need predictable per-token / per-call pricing for budgeting.
- Data residency & auditability: primary production in us-west plus audited logs for compliance reviews.

Primary risks / blockers for adoption
- Procurement wants a short executive summary + clear contracting lane (pilot → SOC2 evidence → MSA signature).
- Legal will request a narrower data processing annex for PII and retention.
- Performance SLA at scale (you asked about 95th <=150ms for the pilot) — we need to confirm baseline and pilot sizing.

What we (Redwood) will deliver by next touch (EOD Thu):
1) One-page board snapshot (attached: redwood-board-snapshot.pdf) tailored to CFO/CTO talking points.
2) Initial SOW draft outlining pilot scope and acceptance criteria (attached: initial-sow-draft-v1.docx).
3) Security pack: SOC 2 summary + privacy brief (I’ve attached the privacy brief in my follow-up).
4) A proposed contracting lane and timeline: pilot kickoff (2–3 weeks after SOW sign), 8-week pilot, measurement review, MSA + reserved capacity proposal.

Immediate asks from you
- Confirm procurement contact who should receive the SOW (name + email) — I think Michael will own procurement.
- Confirm the primary metric for pilot acceptance (is 95th latency <=150ms acceptable as the gate?).
- Any board-level language you want emphasized (cost savings, revenue impact, or reliability?).

Next steps (proposed)
- I’ll share the board one-pager + SOW by Thu.
- Schedule a short 20-min pilot sizing call with your engineering lead next week (I suggested Wed 12/09 and Thu 12/10 below — please confirm).

Attachments: redwood-board-snapshot.pdf, initial-sow-draft-v1.docx

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the board slide if that’s helpful.

—
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Claire Holt <claire.holt@stellarus.com>, Michael Choi <michael.choi@stellarus.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Board snapshot: outcomes and contracting lane

Thanks for the crisp recap, Monica — nice work. Two quick internal flags I want to put on the thread before we send the board packet:

1) SLA / performance ask: Claire, if the CFO is expecting a firm 95th <=150ms SLA for production, we should treat that as an escalation item. Our recommended pilot acceptance gate is a 95th <=200ms with a documented plan to get to 150ms for the reserved deployment (depends on model variant + quantization). I’ll loop in SE for sizing.

2) Contracting lane suggestion: to keep procurement momentum, propose a two-step path in the SOW: (A) pilot SOW + limited trial MSA addendum, (B) follow-on reserved capacity quote + full MSA. That keeps legal review scoped.

Monica — I can draft a one-paragraph SLA caveat that we can include on the board slide calling out pilot vs production targets.

Onward —
Laura
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

- Procurement lead: Michael Choi (michael.choi@stellarus.com) — he’ll manage SOW routing and vendor checks.
- Board ask: CFO wants a 1-pager focused on business impact (revenue upside + cost avoidance) with a simple timeline to signature.
- Data residency: primary requirement is us-west for production; however legal may ask about EU controls for later expansion — include a short note that Redwood supports region pinning.
- SLA: CFO would prefer to see a production SLA target of <=150ms 95th. If you can call out pilot gate at 200ms and a clear plan to 150ms when reserved capacity is in place, that will be acceptable.

We’ve attached a Procurement contacts CSV for routing (procurement-contacts.csv) — please route the SOW to Michael and I’ll coordinate the legal side.

Preferred next steps from Stellarus:

2) Kickoff pilot sizing call next week with SE.
3) Procurement runs vendor checks in parallel — hope to have MSA on the table within 4–6 weeks after pilot acceptance.

Happy to join a 15-min readout with your SE to speed the sizing conversation.
